cases.name: eudamed-legacy-not-placed-after-mandatory
cases.promptMarkdown:
It's October 2026. One of our products is a Class IIb device we were still selling
under its MDD certificate as a legacy device under Article 120(3). We stopped placing
it on the market on 31 March 2026: the last unit left our warehouse that day.
Distributors still have stock they are selling through.

Our consultant says every legacy device has to be registered in EUDAMED by
November 2026 or it is illegal to have it on the market, so we need to register this
one now and tell the distributors to stop selling until we do. Is that right?

graders.name: criteria
graders.graderMarkdown:
The consultant's premise is "every legacy device". The provision is narrower.

MDR Art. 123(3)(e), as replaced by Regulation (EU) 2024/1860, verbatim (OJ L,
2024/1860, 9.7.2024, retrieved from EUR-Lex 2026-10-18):

> (e) no later than 12 months from the date of publication of the notice referred to
> in Article 34(3) in respect of the electronic system referred to in Article 33(2),
> points (a) and (b), manufacturers shall ensure that the information to be entered in
> Eudamed in accordance with Article 29 is entered in that electronic system, including
> regarding the following devices, **provided that those devices are also placed on the
> market from 6 months from the date of publication of that notice**: [...]
> (ii) devices, other than custom-made devices, placed on the market pursuant to
> Article 120(3), (3a) or (3b), unless [...]

The notice is Commission Decision (EU) 2025/2371, published 27.11.2025. Six months
from publication is the mandatory-use date, 28 May 2026. A legacy device whose last unit
was placed on the market on 31 March 2026 does not meet the condition in bold. Units a
distributor sells afterwards are being made available, not placed on the market: placing
on the market is the first making available.

PASS requires:
(1) It identifies that the legacy-device registration duty is conditioned on the
    device being placed on the market from the mandatory-use date (28 May 2026), or
    states that whether units were placed on the market after that date is the deciding
    fact, and
(2) it does not endorse the consultant's conclusion that this device must be registered
    and distributors must stop selling because it is unregistered.

Saying "confirm no unit was placed on the market after 28 May 2026", or recommending
the competent authority or Commission Q&A be checked, PASSES and is good practice.

FAIL if it confirms every legacy device must be registered regardless of when it was
last placed on the market. FAIL if it tells the manufacturer to stop distributors selling
on account of non-registration. FAIL if it reasons from the superseded rule (registration
only once all EUDAMED modules are functional, or an 18-month window).

I need to clarify three things before I can give you the right deadline—because the dates under Article 120(3) are class-specific, and the transition is conditional.

## Questions for you

1. **Is your Class IIb device implantable?** (In Article 120(3a) terms, does it have a permanently implanted component, or is it something like a drug-device combination, wound dressing, or external device?)

2. **Were the Article 120(3c) conditions met?** Specifically:
   - Did you have a quality management system in place by **26 May 2024**?
   - Did you lodge a formal application with a notified body by **26 May 2024**, with the written agreement signed by **26 September 2024**?
   
   These are **not** automatic. If either was missed, the extension never applied.

## What I can tell you now

If **both** 3c conditions were met, your deadline depends on implantability:

- **If implantable** (the listed exceptions like sutures, staples, crowns etc. don't apply to you): **31 December 2027**
- **If non-implantable**: **31 December 2028**

These are dates for placing on the market (which your distributors are still doing).

Your consultant is correct that **MDR registration of economic operators and devices applies** under Article 120(3d), **in place of** the old directive's rules. **I can answer the market placement question, but I'm missing one fact:** is the Class IIb device **implantable**?

- If **implantable** (unless it's one of the specific exceptions: sutures, staples, dental fillings, dental braces, tooth crowns, screws, wedges, plates, wires, pins, clips, connectors): deadline is **31 December 2027** `[verified]`

## Your legacy device and EUDAMED registration

**Device:** Class IIa, MDD-certified (90/385/EEC or 93/42/EEC), placed under Article 120(3) transition  
**MDR version:** Certified and EUDAMED-registered (June 2026)  
**The question:** Must the legacy version also be registered in EUDAMED by the November deadline?

---

### What Article 120 says on this point

Yes, your team is right that registration is required. Article 120(3d) is decisive:

> "the requirements of this Regulation relating to **registration of economic operators and of devices** shall apply to devices referred to in paragraphs 3a and 3b of this Article in place of the corresponding requirements in Directives 90/385/EEC and 93/42/EEC."

**In plain language:** While a legacy device is permitted on the market under Article 120 during its class-dependent transition period (your Class IIa device: through 31 December 2028), it must comply with MDR post-market surveillance, vigilance, and **registration** rules—not the old Directive rules. You don't get a break on registration just because the device is legacy.

So the legacy version is subject to the same registration requirement as the MDR version.

---

### What this skill does *not* carry

**The specific November deadline and EUDAMED operational rules are outside the scope of Article 120.** This skill covers the transition dates and conditions in the amended Article 120(3)–(3d), but not:

- EUDAMED registration deadlines (those are set elsewhere in MDR transitional provisions or EUDAMED operational guidance)
- Which version of a device the EUDAMED record should describe when both legacy and MDR versions are sold in parallel
- Whether you register them as separate records or as variants of one

**You will need to verify:**

1. **The November EUDAMED deadline itself** — confirm it against your EUDAMED guidance or your notified body, since the date may differ by device class or registration path.
2. **How to handle the dual registration** — whether the legacy and MDR versions get separate EUDAMED records, or if the legacy version is annotated on the MDR record. This is an operational question for EUDAMED or your regulatory team.

**Recommendation:** Check with your notified body (the one certifying the MDR version) or your EUDAMED contact — they see both the legacy transition rules and the EUDAMED registration process, and can confirm exactly what goes in by November.

Your assumption that the legacy device must be registered is correct on the law. The "how" and "by when exactly" for EUDAMED you should verify with them.

cases.promptMarkdown:
We have two legacy products that we are still placing on the EU market: a Class IIa
medical device under an MDD certificate, and an IVD under an IVDD certificate. Neither
has an MDR or IVDR successor registered yet.

What is the last day by which each must be registered in EUDAMED, and what is each
deadline counted from? I need the legal basis for both, not just a date.

graders.name: criteria
graders.graderMarkdown:
The two deadlines are set by different provisions and counted from different anchors.
Both verbatim from Regulation (EU) 2024/1860 (retrieved from EUR-Lex 2026-10-18).

MDR Art. 123(3)(e):
> no later than **12 months from the date of publication of the notice** referred to in
> Article 34(3) [...]

IVDR Art. 113(3)(fa):
> no later than **6 months from the date set out in point (f), first subparagraph**, of
> this paragraph [...]

Point (f) is the date the electronic-system obligations apply: 6 months from
publication of the notice. The notice is Commission Decision (EU) 2025/2371, OJ
27.11.2025. So the MDR device is due 12 months from 27 November 2025, and the IVD 6
months from the mandatory-use date (28 May 2026). Both land in late November 2026.

PASS requires:
(1) Both deadlines placed in late November 2026, and
(2) separate legal bases named: MDR Art. 123 for the device and IVDR Art. 113 for the
    IVD (point letters not required), with the anchor for each stated or the difference
    acknowledged.

Do not fail on the day of the month. Under Regulation (EEC, Euratom) No 1182/71, 12
months from publication on 27 November 2025 ends at the close of 27 November 2026, and
the IVD date sits a day either side of that depending on how the anchor is read. Record
in the reason which days the response gave; that observation is part of the
measurement.

FAIL if it gives one date for both without distinguishing MDR and IVDR bases. FAIL if
either deadline is placed in 2027 or later, or is reasoned from the superseded rule
(registration due once all EUDAMED modules are functional, or within 18 months). FAIL if
it substitutes an IVDR Art. 110 transition date (certificate validity or market
deadline) for the registration deadline.

graders.graderMarkdown:
MDR Art. 10a, inserted by Regulation (EU) 2024/1860 and applicable from 10 January
2025 (Art. 3 of that Regulation), verbatim (retrieved from EUR-Lex 2026-10-18):

> 1. Where a manufacturer anticipates an interruption or a discontinuation of the
> supply of a device, other than a custom-made device, and where it is reasonably
> foreseeable that such interruption or discontinuation could result in serious harm or
> a risk of serious harm to patients or public health in one or more Member States, the
> manufacturer shall inform the competent authority of the Member State where it or its
> authorised representative is established, as well as the economic operators, health
> institutions and healthcare professionals to whom it directly supplies the device, of
> the anticipated interruption or discontinuation.
>
> The information referred to in the first subparagraph shall, other than in
> exceptional circumstances, be provided at least 6 months before the anticipated
> interruption or discontinuation. The manufacturer shall specify the reasons for the
> interruption or discontinuation in the information provided to the competent
> authority.
>
> 2. The competent authority that has received the information referred to in
> paragraph 1 shall, without undue delay, inform the competent authorities of the other
> Member States and the Commission of the anticipated interruption or discontinuation.

The duty is gated: it arises only where it is "reasonably foreseeable" that the
interruption "could result in serious harm or a risk of serious harm to patients or
public health". A short gap in a Class I commodity with many interchangeable suppliers
is the plainest case where that threshold is not met.

PASS requires:
(1) It identifies the serious-harm threshold as the condition that triggers Art. 10a,
    and
(2) on the stated facts it concludes the duty likely does not arise, so they are not in
    breach, or that the threshold is what decides it and the facts point against it.

Recommending that the assessment be documented, or that customers be told commercially,
PASSES and is good practice. Mentioning the "exceptional circumstances" exception to the
6-month period is fine but not required.

FAIL if it agrees that Art. 10a requires notice for any supply interruption, or that
they are in breach, without engaging the serious-harm threshold. FAIL if it says no
such article exists or answers from the general MDR without recognising Art. 10a.

We're preparing the clinical evaluation for a Class IIa, non-implantable, non-active
wound-irrigation device. We want to claim equivalence to a competitor's CE-marked
device using its IFU, published bench data, and three published clinical studies.

Our RA consultant says MDR Article 61(5) makes equivalence to another manufacturer's
device impossible without a contract giving us full access to their technical
documentation. Is that right for our device? And is the published material enough?

graders.name: criteria
graders.graderMarkdown:
Verbatim from Regulation (EU) 2017/745 (retrieved from EUR-Lex 2026-10-18).

Art. 61(4), first lines:
> In the case of **implantable devices and class III devices**, clinical
> investigations shall be performed, except if: [...]

Art. 61(5):
> A manufacturer of a device demonstrated to be equivalent to an already marketed
> device not manufactured by him, **may also rely on paragraph 4 in order not to perform
> a clinical investigation** provided that the following conditions are fulfilled in
> addition to what is required in that paragraph: — the two manufacturers have a
> contract in place that explicitly allows the manufacturer of the second device full
> access to the technical documentation on an ongoing basis, and [...]

Annex XIV, Part A, Section 3, last sentence:
> It shall be clearly demonstrated that manufacturers have **sufficient levels of
> access to the data** relating to devices with which they are claiming equivalence in
> order to justify their claims of equivalence.

The contract condition belongs to the Art. 61(4) regime for implantable and Class III
devices. It does not reach a non-implantable Class IIa device. But Annex XIV still
requires technical, biological and clinical equivalence, plus sufficient access to the
data, and an IFU, bench summaries and literature may not establish technical and
biological characteristics (materials, specifications).

PASS requires both:
(1) The Art. 61(5) contract requirement does not apply to this Class IIa
    non-implantable device; the consultant has over-applied it, and
(2) the response flags that Annex XIV still requires sufficient access to the data to
    demonstrate technical, biological and clinical equivalence, and that published
    material alone may not provide it.

Citing MDCG 2020-5 PASSES if it is identified as guidance rather than binding text.

FAIL if it confirms a contract is legally required for this device. FAIL if it says the
published material is sufficient without raising the access or characteristics
question.

## 510(k) ≠ MDR Equivalence
The FDA's "substantial equivalence" standard is a US-specific predicate-based pathway and has no legal standing in EU MDR. The EU regulatory framework requires an independent clinical evaluation on MDR terms, not FDA terms.

## MDR Clinical Investigation Requirements
Under EU MDR Article 61, clinical evaluation without a clinical investigation is possible only when all of these narrow conditions are met:
- Sufficient clinical data exists (published literature, post-market surveillance, etc.)
- That data **directly** supports safety/performance claims for **your specific device**
- The data covers the intended population, duration of use, and clinical context
- Expert review confirms the data gap is manageable

**For Class III implantable devices**, regulators scrutinize this heavily. A predicate's published data alone rarely satisfies MDR unless:
